$comment: Function half of the anon-exposure allow-list, consumed by
scripts/ci/check-anon-exposure-live.mjs alongside `relations`.
SCOPE: SECURITY DEFINER functions in schema public that `anon` can EXECUTE,
excluding trigger functions. SECDEF is the dangerous class because such a
function runs as its OWNER and therefore bypasses RLS entirely — the
table-level protections mean nothing inside one. Non-SECDEF functions run as
the caller, so RLS still applies; there are ~450 of those and gating them
would be noise, not safety.
WHY THIS EXISTS: on 2026-07-30 fn_hostel_unallocated_candidates was found
returning 49 learners — full names, emails, gender, programme, year — to an
unauthenticated caller. SECDEF, no internal guard, a caller-supplied
institution_id. Three more were closed alongside it, two of which WROTE data
(an approval action and a document-number allocator), plus a maintenance job
that deactivated timetables. The table sweep could never have seen any of
them, which is the whole reason this half exists.
A NOTE ON THE FIX THAT ALMOST DID NOT WORK: those functions had no `anon=X`
entry in their ACL at all. anon reached them through PostgreSQL default
EXECUTE grant to PUBLIC, so REVOKE ... FROM anon alone would have changed
nothing while reporting success. For functions, the PUBLIC half of
`FROM anon, PUBLIC` is the load-bearing part.
writes_data is a TEXT HEURISTIC over the function body, not proof — it also
matches things like updated_at. It is recorded so that a grandfathered write
can be ESCALATED rather than warned: an unauthenticated write path should
never sit quietly on a warning list.

Correction 2026-07-30: an earlier version of this file listed fn_update_recruitment_step_comment among the writers that "raise on a permission check before touching a row". That claim is WRONG — its guard evaluates to NULL for an anonymous caller and falls through to the UPDATE. The earlier test that cleared it used a non-existent candidate id and stopped at a "Candidate not found" raise several lines BEFORE the authorization check, which was therefore never exercised. Separately, eight anon-readable functions (3 returning real people and the super-admin list, 5 exposing platform settings including 3 live Meta webhook credentials) were revoked on 2026-07-30 and their entries deleted from this file.

2026-07-31: removed get_billing_analytics_by_category and get_billing_collection_split — the live sweep reported both as no longer anon-executable, so their entries were describing a grant that no longer exists.

2026-08-13: the sweep reported 8 unapproved functions. SIX are being REVOKED by supabase/migrations/20260827020000_revoke_anon_execute_six_secdef.sql (the five hr shift-timing / leave-balance RPCs, which take the staff or institution they report on AS A PARAMETER — the same shape that leaked 49 learners on 07-30 — plus tms_expire_stale_trips, which had no guard at all and expires every active trip cluster-wide). They are deliberately NOT listed here: a revoke removes them from the sweep's input, and adding them would leave two stale entries behind. The remaining TWO, fn_is_event_creator and fn_is_designated_leave_approver, are approved below because revoking them would BREAK production rather than protect it — see their reasons. Until that migration is applied (it is Director-gated), this sweep stays red on those six, which is correct: the exposure is real and still open.

2026-08-13, worth knowing before trusting the writes_data column: it under-reports in TWO independent ways, both measured on production. (1) CASE — the UPDATE arm of the heuristic is the POSIX `~` operator, not `~*`, while its `insert into` / `delete from` siblings use ILIKE. tms_expire_stale_trips writes `update public.tms_trip` in lowercase, so it matched `~ 'UPDATE[[:space:]]+public\.'` = false and `~* ...` = true. The single most destructive function on the list was therefore classified `reads`. (2) INDIRECTION — generate_hr_leave_balances_bulk contains no DML text at all; it writes by calling public.generate_hr_leave_balances() once per organisation inside a loop, so every arm of the heuristic returns false. Both would have landed in fnWarned rather than fnEscalated had anyone grandfathered them. The header already says writes_data is a heuristic and not proof; these are the two concrete shapes it misses.

functions.name: fn_is_designated_leave_approver
functions.reason: DO NOT REVOKE — two independent reasons, both verified live 2026-08-13. (a) ZERO EXPOSURE: the body derives its entire answer from auth.uid(), which is NULL for anon, and it takes no caller-supplied identity — its only argument is the leave application to test, never a person. Its guard lines read `AND auth.uid() IS NOT NULL`, `NULLIF(s.step->>'approver_user_id','')::uuid = auth.uid()` and `WHERE ur.user_id = auth.uid()`, so an unauthenticated caller can only ever get false. (b) REVOKING BREAKS PRODUCTION: it appears in RLS policies hla_select and hla_update on hr_leave_applications, both with role PUBLIC. A function called inside an RLS policy is evaluated as the QUERYING role, so removing anon's EXECUTE makes anon queries raise `permission denied for function` instead of returning zero rows. This entry exists so the sweep stops flagging it and the next engineer does not 'fix' it into an outage.

functions.name: fn_is_event_creator
functions.reason: DO NOT REVOKE — two independent reasons, both verified live 2026-08-13. (a) ZERO EXPOSURE: its whole body is `AND e.created_by = (SELECT auth.uid())`, which is NULL for anon; it takes the event to test, never a person, so an unauthenticated caller can only ever get false. (b) REVOKING BREAKS PRODUCTION: it appears in RLS policies event_registration_forms_manage, event_registration_form_sections_manage and event_registration_form_fields_manage, all with role PUBLIC. A function called inside an RLS policy is evaluated as the QUERYING role, so removing anon's EXECUTE makes anon queries raise `permission denied for function` instead of returning zero rows — and that would break the public event-registration form, which is School of Influence's own application front door. This entry exists so the sweep stops flagging it and the next engineer does not 'fix' it into an outage.
